name: MN-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District fundamentals: D+18 partisan lean in a Twin Cities-area seat
McCollum's incumbency and roughly 20-to-1 fundraising edge ($1.45M vs $63K)
Prediction markets price McCollum near 96% to win
No competitive polling or outside spending signals any threat
model.rationale: The district's D+18 lean, McCollum's long incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of more than twenty to one leave Paul Wikstrom without a visible path; markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: Only a major late development involving the incumbent or an extraordinary national shift toward Republicans would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's fourth district, covering St. Paul and its eastern suburbs, leans heavily Democratic, and Betty McCollum has held the seat since 2001. She is running again after securing renomination, with about $497,000 on hand after raising $1.4 million. Republican Paul Wikstrom has raised roughly $62,000 and enters the general election with little visibility or financial backing.

No public general-election polling tracks the race, and no outside groups are spending on either side, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the incumbent's resources. Prediction markets put McCollum's chances near 96 percent. An expected margin in the low twenties leaves only a narrow path for an upset, and the seat is rated Safe Democratic with high confidence.
